case_name: Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States Regulation
issues: Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States Regulation and Prohibition must be distinguished from each other
holding: Notwithstanding anything in Article 301 or Article 303, the Legislature of a State may by law impose on goods imported from other States any tax to which similar goods manufactured or produced in that State are subject, so however as not to discriminate between goods so imported and goods so manufactured or produced; and (b) impose such reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse with or within that State as may be required in the public interests: Provided that no Bill or amendment for the purposes of clause (b) shall be introduced or moved in the Legislature of a State without the previous sanction of the President.
